title: Diction
description: French diction.
prerequisites_raw: Primarily for Voice majors. Music 25 or equivalent.

title: Form and Analysis of Classical Music
description: Analysis of small- and large-scale formal structures in music from the late Baroque through the late Classic period (ca. 1720-1820).
prerequisites_raw: Music 4C; Music 5C with a grade of at least C-.

title: Twentieth Century Analysis
description: Analysis of non-tonal and twelve-tone music.
prerequisites_raw: Music 4C; Music 5C with a grade of at least C-.

title: Advanced Tonal Analysis
description: Continuation of Music 160A, advanced tonal analysis through nineteenth century works.

title: Tuning and Temperament
description: Survey of a number of tuning systems found around the world, including those of Ancient Greece, Europe, India, China, the Arab Middle East, Turkey, and Indonesia. The mathematical, aesthetic, and symbolic bases of each system will be considered.

title: The Arabic System of Melodic Modes: The Maqamat
description: An intensive examination of the system of melodic modes (Maqamat) that governs present-day practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordel structures, and theories of intonation), analysis of standard repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

title: Sound Color: Timbre and Music
description: "Sound color" refers to the quality or timbre of musical sound, whether instrumental, vocal, or synthetic. This course investigates timbre's special perceptual and cognitive qualities, as well as its unique expressive power in music.

title: Analysis of Popular Music
description: Explores different approaches to analyzing popular music (specifically post-1960, predominantly American popular music), including not only theory and analysis of harmony and melody, form, timbre, rhythm/meter but also issues of meanings and expression, intertextuality, race and gender.
prerequisites_raw: Music 5B with a grade of at least C-

title: Keyboard Literature
description: A comprehensive survey of the history and development of stringed keyboard instruments and the repertoire associated with these diverse instruments. An extensive listening list will be available via the Naxos Music Library.
prerequisites_raw: Music 11 or Music 5A; Music 10A, or Music 10B, or Music 10COR WITH CONSENT OF INSTRUCTOR.

title: Choral Literature
description: A historical and analytical survey of major choral works from the seventeenth century to the present.
prerequisites_raw: Three quarters of the Music 112A-F series.

title: Popular Music & Globalization
description: Through the interface of globalization and music, we will explore the cultural politics of nation and person, community and commodity, in modern societies, as well as the ways recording and broadcasts of music have changed musical practices and experiences.

title: Music and Religion
description: An examination of the structural role and symbolic functions of music in religious systems. Case studies will be drawn from diverse world traditions.

title: Other Issues in Ethnomusicology
description: A study of other cultural issues in ethnomusicology. Specific issue or topics will vary by quarter and will be announced in advance by the department.

title: Music and Tourism
description: Students read folklore, anthropology, tourism studies, musicology, and ethnomusicology in an attempt to develop theories for interpreting the impact of tourism on music locally and globally.

title: Film Music Cognition
description: A consideration of film music as a medium of communication between the director, composer, music supervisor, editors, performers and the audience. Emphasis given to cognitive psychological theories of meaning in terms of structure and affect in audio/visual contexts.

title: Music and Documentary Film
description: View global popular music through the lens of documentary film. We will analyze a series of films depicting cultural and political histories, creative performances, and everyday lives of musicians in different representational frames and social contexts.

title: The Musical World of the Grateful Dead: from Americana to Psychedelia
description: An examination of the Grateful Dead and its impact on popular culture, festivals and the music business. We study the Dead’s music from folk to improvisational rock as a creative Americana response to the political turbulence of the Sixties.

title: Music as Media
description: Recorded media are central to the way we hear, create, exchange and experience music in contemporary social life. Topics include the early uses of the phonograph, recording studios, file-sharing, online musical exchange and roles of technological media in globalizing cultures.

title: Creative Arts, Memories and Experimental Performance
description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.

title: History and Practice of the Recording Studio
description: Explores contemporary histories and techniques of the recording studio, focusing on the role of sound engineers in US/UK postwar popular music. In addition to exploring the history of recorded sound, the class will provide students with opportunities to learn practical methods of music production.

title: Music and Sports
description: In this course, students study connections between the human cultural practices of music and sport. We draw from rich literatures in performance studies, sports studies, and ethnomusicology to consider selected case studies where music and sport intersect.

title: Birds, sonic arts & environmental sensitivities
description: Focusing on birds and sonic arts, this course engages creative, analytical & experiential activities. Topics include: ecoacoustics, sound maps, deep listening, sensory memory, soundscape ecologies and environmental issues, blurring borders between more-than-human/human interactions, art/science, and local/global.

title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music, Her Life, Her Times
description: Analysis of the music, life, an times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance practice, and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

title: Notation and Transcription in Ethnomusicology
description: Survey of existing notational systems and exercises in ethnomusicological transcription, with particular attention to issues related to the visual representation of performed musical sound.

title: Musical Acoustics
description: Consideration of the relationships between acoustics, perception and music. Emphasis on the physical and psychophysiological bases for tonality, dynamics, timbre and rhythm. Additional focus on the vibrational properties of musical instruments and features of digital recording and playback.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; Music 11 or Music 5A (which may be concurrent).

title: Understanding Brazilian Music in its Cultural Context
description: This course enables students to understand what Brazilian music is, and what is the role of Music in Brazilian culture. It offers a comprehensive panel of the history of music in Brazil. The course also provides students with a full cultural context, discussing the role of music during the two dictatorship periods in Brazil, 1930-1945 and 1964-1985 and the political impact of censorship. It also discusses the contributions of the Africans, brought to Brazil by the Portuguese colonizers, and the impact African culture has both in music and religion. Taught in English.

title: Music Cultures of the World: China
description: An examination of universal music issues through case studies of Chinese musical works, musicians, theories, and practices. Special attention given to interdisciplinary understanding of Chinese music and culture.

title: Music Cultures of the World: The Middle East
description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.

title: Music Cultures of the World: India
description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis on the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rhythmic structures (Raga and Tala).
